Certificate Install Process

Download and install the GP environment certificate (idm4.grameenphone.com) so RemoteApp stops warning about an untrusted certificate.

ADownload · 2 steps
BInstall · 4 steps
✓Open browser from IAM (IDM3 / IDM4)

A · Download the certificate

STEP1

Open Details and copy the Issuer

In the RemoteApp warning click View certificate…, open the Details tab, select Issuer and click Copy to File….

STEP2

Run the Certificate Export Wizard

Hit Next and Next, then use Browse to keep the certificate in your desired path.

Result: the certificate is saved as a .cer file (for example abc.cer on the Desktop).

B · Install the certificate

STEP1

Double-click the certificate

Locate the downloaded .cer file and double-click it.

STEP2

Click Install Certificate

On the General tab click Install Certificate…, then Next with Current User selected.

STEP3

Place the certificate in Trusted Root

Choose Place all certificates in the following store → Browse… → Trusted Root Certification Authorities.

STEP4

Finish the installation

Click Next and Next, then Finish to install the certificate.

You are done. Open your browser from IAM (IDM3 or IDM4) and you will be connected to the GP environment.

Password Reset, Account Unlock & Change Password

Holmes – Credential Administrator (legacy AD ID) user procedure, OTP based

3procedures
OTPmobile / email check
3344IT Service Desk VOIP
Intranethttps://isupport.grameenphone.com
Internethttps://webserv.grameenphone.com/CredAdmin/Home/NewLogin/
Note: the user mobile number must be updated in Outlook (Mobile Number attribute), otherwise the OTP cannot be delivered.

Use Password Reset when: the password is expired · the user forgot the password · the user thinks someone else is using the account.

Open the Credential Administrator URL in a browser and use Account Unlock / Password Reset on the login page.

A · Password Reset

STEP1

Open Account Unlock / Password Reset

Click “AD Account unlock and Password reset” on the login page.

STEP2

Verify the user

Enter the User ID and the captcha text, then click Verify. An OTP is sent to the registered mobile number / email.

STEP3

Validate the OTP

Enter the received OTP and click Validate. A wrong OTP shows an error: enter the correct one or click Regenerate OTP.

STEP4

Reset the password

If the account is not locked, click Reset Password. Enter the new password, confirm it as per the policy and click Reset Password.

STEP5

Confirm

A success message is shown. Close the window.

Password policy: (1) no part of your full name longer than two consecutive characters · (2) minimum 8 characters · (3) at least three of: upper-case A–Z, lower-case a–z, numbers 0–9, special characters (! $ # %).

B · Account Unlock

If the account is locked the login page shows “Your account is locked”. Click Account Unlock / Password Reset.

STEP1

Verify the user

Enter User ID and captcha text and click Verify.

STEP2

Enter the OTP

The OTP arrives on the registered mobile. Enter it and click Validate.

STEP3

Account unlocked

A confirmation is shown. If required, click Reset Password and proceed as in part A.

C · Change Password

Use Change Password when: the password is going to expire · the user knows the password but cannot sign in · the user thinks someone else is using the account. Log in with User ID, password and captcha first.

STEP1

Click Change Password

Click the “Change Password” button on the Home page.

STEP2

Enter the passwords

Enter Current Password, New Password and the same Confirm Password, then click Change.

STEP✓

Success

The success message is displayed.

Need help? VOIP 3344 · Email it.servicedesk@grameenphone.com

User Account Creation Process

Create AD users on Legacy and DA, then complete the properties by account type

8creation steps
5account types
2directories: Legacy & DA

A · Create the user

STEP1

Log in to the GP Jump host

Use the credentials of Domain\account.

STEP2

Open Active Directory Users and Computers

Search Administrative Tools, then select Active Directory Users and Computers.

STEP3

Go to the temporary OU

Put the new account in the temporary OU “Z” on Legacy and OU “test” on DA. Expand the grameenphone.com domain and click the OU.

STEP4

New → User

Right-click the right pane, choose New, then User.

STEP5

Fill the required fields

Enter First name, Last name, Full name and User logon name.

STEP6

Set the password

Click Next. The password must meet complexity rules with a minimum of 16 characters, and “User must change password at next logon” must be ticked.

STEP7

Finish

Click Next and Finish. The user is now created in OU “Z” (Legacy) / OU “test” (DA).

STEP8

Open the user Properties

Update the information in the tabs, according to the account type below.

Keep in mind: Full name and User logon name must be the same · User logon name limit is 20 characters · always use small letters for the User logon name.

C · Attribute Editor walkthrough (DA only)

STEP1

Enable Advanced Features

In ADUC choose View and make sure Advanced Features is ticked.

STEP2

Create a Saved Query

Right-click Saved Queries → New → Query, give it any name and click Define Query.

STEP3

Define the query

On the Users tab set Name to “Has a value”, click OK and OK again.

STEP4

Open the user Properties

Expand Saved Queries, open your query, find the user and open Properties.

STEP5

Edit the attributes

On the Attribute Editor tab double-click an attribute, paste the value and click OK.

DA Jump Host Access

Reach the DA jump host over RDP after connecting to the GNDC network

5steps

Open Remote Desktop Connection

Enter the service JH IP and port (192.168.120.229:5508 or 192.168.120.233) as the computer name and click Connect.

STEP2

Enter your DA AD ID

Give the username (format grameenphone\wipro.zahidul) and the password of your DA AD ID, then click OK.

Accept the warning

You are in

TSS Ticketing Tool: Ticket Raise SOP

Raise, track and follow up TSS tickets on behalf of a Grameenphone user

22steps
SR / Incidentchoose the right type
TSS Ticket Mailsub-folder for updates
Portalhttps://telenorpeopleportal.service-now.com
Usernameericsson.gss.user1@grameenphone.com
Password•••••••••• (click to show)
Remember: without a Grameenphone employee email address you cannot raise any TSS ticket.

A · Log in and open the catalog

STEP1

Open the TSS tool

Open the portal link in a browser and enter the username above.

STEP2

Password and approval

Enter the password. A mobile authentication notification goes to the SD person / NOC mobile: approve it and you are logged in.

STEP3

Home page

After login the People Portal home page looks like this.

STEP4

Open the IT menu

Click “IT” at the top left. Mostly used: IT › Microsoft 365 › Email, Login & MFA, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and Intel (from Other).

STEP5

Pick the catalog and type

Select the catalog (e.g. Email). For an SR choose “Email/Outlook related request”; for an Incident choose “Email/Outlook issue”.

B · Fill in and submit the ticket

STEP6

Requested for

In the ticket form use the “Requested for” field to set the ticket requester.

STEP7

Save the user mail as .eml

From the user mail choose Download → Download as EML and keep it on Desktop / Downloads.

STEP8

Mail saved

The mail file is saved in the folder.

STEP9

Copy the user email address

Copy the user email from the contact card.

STEP10

Paste into Requested for

Paste the GP user email, then select his name. The user details are filled in.

STEP11

Select the sub-category

Choose the request type that matches the user mail description.

STEP12

Request details

Copy the request from the mail body and paste it into “Request details”, or type it yourself after talking to the user.

Add attachments

Glossary

Terms used across the SOPs.

Output and outcome

Output is what a service delivers (a password reset). Outcome is the result for the consumer (they can work).

Utility and warranty

Utility is what a service does (fit for purpose). Warranty is how well it performs (fit for use).

Service value chain

The six ITIL activities: plan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain or build, deliver and support.

Known error

A problem that has been analyzed but not resolved, usually with a documented workaround.

Standard change

A pre-authorized, low-risk, well-understood change in ITIL.

RTO and RPO

RTO is how fast a service must be back. RPO is how much data loss is acceptable, measured in time.

802.1X

Port-based network access control with a supplicant (device), an authenticator (switch or access point) and an authentication server (RADIUS).

3-2-1 backup rule

Keep three copies of data, on two kinds of media, with one copy off site.

CIDR / prefix length

The number after the slash in an address such as 192.168.10.0/24. It says how many bits belong to the network.

Subnet mask

Dotted form of the prefix length. A /24 is 255.255.255.0.

VLAN

A virtual LAN: one switch is split into separate broadcast networks, tagged with 802.1Q on trunk links.

Shared responsibility model

Cloud rule of who secures what: the provider secures the cloud itself, the customer secures what runs in it.

Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft's cloud identity service (the new name of Azure AD): users, groups, MFA, SSPR and Conditional Access.

Exam domain

A topic area of a certification exam with a percentage weight, for example Network Security 14%.

DA

Newer AD environment. Password reset at daisupport.grameenphone.com; used for PC login, O365, VPN and DA jump hosts.

Legacy

Older AD environment. Password at webserv.grameenphone.com; used for CIMS, Cockpit, CCPS and Legacy jump hosts.

AD / ADUC

Active Directory and the Active Directory Users and Computers console used to create and edit users.

OU

Organizational Unit: the AD folder where a user account is placed, based on designation or account type.

SamAccountName

The user logon name, e.g. firstname.lastname. Limit 20 characters, small letters.

SSPR

Self-Service Password Reset. Portal access comes from group GL-GP-SSPR-Users.

MFA

Multi-factor authentication: a second approval, e.g. a notification on the SD/NOC mobile when logging in to TSS.

OTP

One-time password sent to the registered mobile / email by Holmes Credential Administrator.

Holmes (Credential Administrator)

The self-service tool to reset a password, unlock an account or change a password using OTP.

GAL

Global Address List. Holmes has a GAL Modification option.

JH / Jump host

A server you reach by RDP first, then use to access other systems (DA and Legacy jump hosts).

RDP

Remote Desktop Protocol: the Remote Desktop Connection app.

VPN / GlobalProtect

The VPN client (C2S) used to reach the GNDC network before opening the jump host.

TSS

The ticketing tool at telenorpeopleportal.service-now.com used to raise tickets for GP users.

Summit

The service desk ticketing tool whose SR catalog and workgroups are listed in the SR Catalog Update page.

SD / NOC

Service Desk and Network Operations Centre teams that raise and approve tickets.

Catalog / Catalog-2

The path chosen in the ticket tool to classify the request. Catalog-2 is the specific item.

Workgroup

The team a ticket is assigned to in Summit.

UAT

User Acceptance Testing: the new Platforms SR catalog stays in UAT until GP's go-live mail.

EML

Email file format used to attach the user's original mail to a TSS ticket.

E3 / E5

Microsoft 365 licence levels, given via GL-GP-O365-default-Users (E3) and GL-GP-O365-advance-Users (E5).

proxyAddresses

AD attribute holding the email alias, e.g. SMTP:a.anwar@grameenphone.com.

Certificate store

Windows area where certificates are kept. The SOP installs into Trusted Root Certification Authorities.

L1 / L2

First and second level support; used in the SR catalog domain descriptions.

RITM

Request item number of a TSS ticket, e.g. RITM0099661.

SR number

Summit ticket number, e.g. SR302959.

AD Sync

Time a new mail group (DL) needs to sync into AD before members can be added.

DL

Distribution list: an Office 365 mail group created by self-service.

CIM / CIMS

Tool that uses the Legacy password. After a Legacy reset the password is changed twice before login.

Online Archive

Mailbox archive. Auto-online archive is enabled by raising a TSS ticket.

SD Handover

End-of-shift note: scope, major issues and special instructions for the next shift.

GP Spoke Person

The GP contact whose email is needed to raise an SR on behalf of an outside requester.

SR (Service Request)

User is asking for something new, or a formal request for a standard service. Examples: password reset, install an application, access needed.

INC (Incident)

Something has happened and needs to be fixed: a service interruption, or an unplanned interruption or reduction of service. Example: Outlook is not opening.

Work Order

The actual task assigned to a technical team to perform the work.

SLA

Service Level Agreement: a formal agreement on how fast the service desk will respond to and resolve the issue.

Ticket Priority (P1–P4)

P1: 4 hours (240 min), service window 24×7 P2: 8 hours (480 min), service window 24×7 P3: 12 hours (720 min), service window 16×7 P4: 24 hours (1440 min), service window 8×5

DMS (Distribution Management System)

Application that manages how products such as SIMs, recharge cards and devices move from the company to distributors and retail points: orders, stock, sales and settlement. Seen in: SR Catalog Update, workgroup DMS.

RMS (Retail Management System)

Application that runs retail outlet operations: point-of-sale, stock at the shop, sales records and customer service at the counter. Seen in: SR Catalog Update, workgroup Retail Management System (RMS).

NMS (Network Management System)

System that monitors and manages network devices: alarms and faults, performance and configuration. Used by network teams to see problems early. Typical use: network health monitoring.

CRM (Customer Relationship Management)

System that keeps customer details, history and interactions (requests, complaints, cases) so that teams can serve each customer consistently. Seen in: SR Catalog Update, CRM Solutions (GPCIM-Support).

CMP (Contextual Marketing Platform)

Marketing platform that sends the right offer to the right customer at the right moment, based on context such as usage, location or time. Seen in: SR Catalog Update, workgroup CMP Pelatro.

MNP (Mobile Number Portability)

Service that lets a subscriber keep the same mobile number when switching from one operator to another.

DPDP (Digital Platform Delivery Platform)

Expansion as given by the team: a platform used to deliver digital services. Ask the owning team for the exact scope.

Which jump host?

Legacy account: jump host 8 (192.168.158.8) DA AD account: jump host 229 (192.168.120.229:5508)

IT Service Desk number

3344

IM / AM (Tower)

In the pending report, every workgroup belongs to a Tower: IM (Infrastructure Management) or AM (Application Management). The Tower comes from the workgroup mapping sheet.

Age Count

Age bucket of a pending ticket: 24 Hours, 2 Days, 3 Days, 4 Days, 5 Days or Above 5 Days, based on working days since the log time.

WH Without Weekend

Working time elapsed since the ticket was logged until the report date, not counting Friday and Saturday.

Pending report

Daily morning report of pending incidents (INC) and service requests (SR) by Tower, workgroup and age. See the Daily Report page.

Resolved at last day

Second table of the morning mail: number of INC and SR resolved on the previous working day, per workgroup, with a Grand Total.

Pending vs resolved statuses

Pending by age counts tickets in In-Progress or Pending status. The resolved table counts tickets in Resolved or Closed status on the last working day.

SR Catalog Location

Where a workgroup's service requests are raised in the Summit tool, for example Application Management\CRM Solutions or PLATFORMS\EUC. See the Workgroup Directory page.

DWE

Short name of the Dynamic Workflow Engine workgroup.

Shorborno

IT Security domain with the workgroups IR, PT, SOC, tools and VA. SR catalog \\SHORBORNO covers security alerts, VM scan, virus attack and vulnerability check/scan.

Executor team

Team that executes an SR, written in the SR Executor Team column of the SR status mail. It is set per workgroup in the Workgroup Directory (for example ESL Network Admin shows as ESL Network Admin & Security, NOC as ITSM-NOC).
